policy: These are research requests and scope seeds. They are not completed engineering maps, endorsements, or claims of access to proprietary designs. Populate detailed components and interfaces only with cited evidence; label analytical inferences explicitly.

included: Agency systems-engineering lifecycle and governance
Mission architecture and system boundaries
ConOps, stakeholder expectations and requirements flowdown
Functional, logical and physical architecture views
Subsystem interfaces and interface control
Ground systems, spacecraft, launch services and mission operations
Verification, validation, integration and technical reviews
Model-based systems engineering and SysML work products
Safety, reliability, risk and configuration management
excluded: Export-controlled or restricted technical data without authorization

research_questions: How does NASA tailor systems-engineering rigor across mission classes and lifecycle phases?
How are requirements traced from stakeholder expectations through subsystem allocation and verification evidence?
Which architecture views and model artifacts are used to describe functions, components, interfaces and operational modes?
How are ground, flight, launch, communications and mission-operations interfaces governed?
How do hazard analysis, reliability, configuration management and technical reviews connect to design baselines?

initial_evidence.claim_or_artifact: NASA Systems Engineering Handbook covering program/project lifecycle, system design, product realization and technical management.
NASA Procedural Requirements 7123.1D, Systems Engineering Processes and Requirements; effective 2023-07-05, expiration 2028-07-05 as listed on the directive page.
Systems Modeling Handbook describing model planning, model organization, SysML examples and generation of systems-engineering work products.

deliverables: Representative mission system context and functional maps
Safety, risk and configuration evidence map
open_questions: Select representative mission programs for deep component-level maps.
Identify public model artifacts, interface documents and mission data products by mission.

included: Falcon 9 launch vehicle and reusable first-stage architecture
Starship and Super Heavy integrated transportation system
Propulsion, structures, tanks, avionics, flight software and ground support
Launch site, pad, integration, countdown and range interfaces
Payload integration and mission operations
Recovery, refurbishment, reuse and lifecycle economics
Publicly documented Starlink system interfaces where evidence supports mapping
excluded: Proprietary detailed drawings, source code, restricted operational procedures and export-controlled technical data

research_questions: What public evidence establishes system boundaries and stage/subsystem decomposition for Falcon 9 and Starship?
How do propulsion, structures, avionics, flight software, ground systems and payload interfaces connect?
What are the documented launch, ascent, separation, recovery and refurbishment flows?
Which performance values are vehicle-configuration-specific and revision-dated?
How are public safety, reliability, reuse and mission assurance claims supported by evidence?

initial_evidence.claim_or_artifact: Official Starship overview describes Starship and Super Heavy as a fully reusable transportation system and provides high-level vehicle specifications.
Official Falcon 9 overview describes a reusable two-stage launch vehicle and publishes first-stage propulsion and vehicle-level specifications.
Launch and mission pages are candidate evidence for mission profiles; resolve current payload user guides and revisions during discovery.

deliverables: Falcon 9 system decomposition and mission sequence map
open_questions: Resolve current official user guides and revision identifiers for each vehicle and payload interface.
Determine which launch-site, ground-support and operational details are publicly documented at useful engineering depth.

subject.name: Tesla vehicle, energy, AI and manufacturing systems

included: Vehicle platform architecture: structure, body, battery, power electronics, thermal, drive, charging and software
Battery cell, pack, battery-management and thermal-safety architecture
Energy generation/storage products and grid interconnection
Powerwall, Megapack and publicly documented control/software platforms
Autonomy/robotics compute and public software/AI infrastructure disclosures
Factory systems: materials, automation, robotics, quality, test and production flows
Supply chain, service, charging, recycling and product lifecycle
excluded: Private vehicle firmware/source code, proprietary CAD, factory control networks, customer personal data and restricted supplier data

research_questions: How do publicly disclosed vehicle subsystems integrate across structural, electrical, thermal, propulsion and software domains?
What evidence describes cell-to-pack design, battery management, thermal control, fault containment and validation?
How do energy storage hardware, power electronics, grid interfaces and dispatch software form an end-to-end system?
What public evidence maps manufacturing automation, robotics, factory simulation, quality inspection and material flows?
How are vehicle/energy field data, compute infrastructure, model training and deployed software described in public disclosures?
What lifecycle flows connect materials sourcing, manufacturing, service, reuse and recycling?

initial_evidence.claim_or_artifact: Official investor-relations archive for annual and quarterly filings, shareholder updates and impact reports.
Official manufacturing overview describes factory footprint, vehicle/battery production and factory automation.
Official battery engineering article describes cell/pack integration, thermal management, cell inspection and battery safety claims.
Extended Impact Report includes energy manufacturing, battery production and product/safety disclosures; use revision-specific evidence locators.

deliverables: Vehicle system context and subsystem maps
Factory production and automation value-stream map
AI/compute/data lifecycle map based on public disclosures
Supply-chain, service and recycling lifecycle map
open_questions: Select vehicle platform generations and variants for comparison.
Identify current public technical documents for charging, energy dispatch, autonomy compute and manufacturing systems.
Separate company-reported claims from independently verified performance and safety evidence.
